A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VFlowOpt research. All 13 pages in each version, including figures, tables, equations, and supplementary Sections A–D, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image and video benchmark evaluations, efficiency measurements, component ablations, and optimization analyses in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–4 and supplementary efficiency and ablation results in Tables 7–10.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain identical attention-and-entropy importance estimation, progressive pruning, token recycling, and Bayesian optimization using final-token similarity. No method component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten image benchmarks and SeedBench/VideoMME video tasks. Appendix D.2 also retains the same optimization-data comparison involving random training samples and MathV360K-Geometry3K.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains FastV, SparseVLM, and VisionZip; Tables 2–4 and 7 retain FastV and VisionZip, and Table 8 retains VisionZip. The newly cited AuroraCap and CATP are not added to any evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: The model configurations, token-retention budgets, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures are unchanged. Section 4.1 retains 30 unlabeled optimization samples and 50 Bayesian optimization iterations, with the same model-specific pruning locations.

E4.justification: Both retain the component ablations in Tables 6 and 10, sample/iteration sensitivity in Figure 4, information-flow case study in Figure 5, optimization-data comparison in Table 8, and optimization-target comparison in Table 9.

E5.justification: Appendix D.2 retains the same qualitative statement that repeated random sampling yields nearly identical results. Neither version provides additional run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries, numerical values, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, at 10% token retention, Table 1 reports 85.5% retained average performance and Table 4 reports 95.5% for video in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain identical definitions and mathematical objectives, including token importance, average retention rate, weighted token merging, and final-token cosine similarity. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and efficiency/generalization claims, including 90% visual-token pruning, an 89% KV-cache reduction, and 3.8× faster inference.

C2.justification: The explanations linking final-token similarity to preserved visual information and interpreting component contributions remain identical. Appendix D retains its data-independence argument and semantic interpretations of ablations; no limitations or qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same pruning layers, pixel cap, importance-map transformations, optimization settings, A100 hardware, and approximate optimization time. The printed code-access link is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds citations to AuroraCap and CATP in its opening token-reduction statement, introducing references 5 and 23 in v2. All 54 previous reference entries remain; the research positioning and discussion of existing methods are otherwise unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes are limited to citation insertion and renumbering and the updated arXiv version/date header. Narrative wording, terminology, section ordering, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citations and bibliography entries cause limited text reflow in Section 2.2 and the reference pages. Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–10 retain their content, formatting, captions, and placement.

improvement.justification: The two added citations modestly broaden attribution in Section 2.2 but receive no accompanying analysis or comparison. The method, empirical evidence, explanations, and reproducibility information—including all appendix analyses—remain unchanged, with no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
